headline: High-risk data leakage and capability conflict: Replit Agent’s secret-bearing workspace plus broad egress can expose Plandex outputs and code by default.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Plandex reads and writes a project directory with review-then-apply, while Replit Agent operates in a persistent Repl workspace and can act on files. A shared filesystem-style bridge makes file content a plausible instruction channel, though no MCP or clipboard bridge is shown. The interaction is documented enough to avoid higher severity, but not enough to rule it out.
conditions: IF the same workspace files are visible to both agents, file content can steer downstream actions.
IF either agent treats workspace text as instructions without provenance checks, injection becomes actionable.
mitigations: Separate the agents into different directories.
Require a human review step before applying any file-derived instruction.
Prefix untrusted file content as data, not commands.
Disable auto-apply modes during cross-agent workflows.

B_data_leakage.rationale: Plandex touches source code and can call external model providers; Replit Agent touches source code, secrets, and deployment configuration, with broad network egress and persistent Repl files. If they share a workspace or hand off files, sensitive material from Replit can flow into Plandex outputs or third-party APIs. The blast radius includes secrets and code, so this is high.
conditions: IF both agents access the same project files, secrets may be exposed to the other agent's context.
IF Plandex sends file contents to its model provider, Replit secrets or deployment config can leave the workspace.
mitigations: Keep secrets out of any shared directory.
Use separate workspaces for the two agents.
Redact .env and secret files before either agent runs.
Restrict outbound access for the agent handling sensitive files.
Rotate any secrets touched during a shared-session test.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Both agents can write the filesystem, modify git state, execute shells, and spawn subprocesses. Plandex has shared state via a Plandex server backend, while Replit Agent has persistent Repl filesystem state. Concurrent edits to the same repo or git branch can overwrite each other without locking, matching the high-risk overlap pattern.
conditions: IF both agents operate on the same git branch or directory, concurrent writes can conflict.
IF either agent auto-applies changes while the other is editing, state corruption becomes likely.
mitigations: Assign each agent a separate branch.
Serialize write access with a human gate.
Disable auto-apply on at least one agent.
Snapshot the workspace before parallel runs.
Merge changes only after diff review.

D_cascading_error.rationale: Plandex uses a review-then-apply workflow, but Replit Agent acts inside the Repl with user checkpoints and can execute tool calls. If Plandex output is copied into Replit Agent as authoritative task text, the second agent may act on unverified instructions. The pathway exists, but both profiles show some checkpointing, so medium fits.
conditions: IF Plandex-generated text is fed directly into Replit Agent as instructions, errors can cascade.
IF Replit Agent is allowed to execute shell actions from unverified summaries, downstream mistakes can propagate.
mitigations: Require a verification step between agents.
Pass only structured diffs, not free-form instructions.
Have a human confirm any action plan before execution.
Compare outputs against the original task before applying.

E_compliance.rationale: Replit Agent explicitly touches secrets and deployment configuration, while Plandex handles source code and can send content to a model provider. If regulated or sensitive deployment data is placed in the Replit workspace and then processed by Plandex, retention and residency expectations may diverge. The profiles do not show a specific jurisdiction mismatch, so medium is the highest supportable level.
conditions: IF regulated secrets or deployment configuration are stored in the Replit workspace, compliance review is required before sharing with Plandex.
IF either agent retains prompts or file contents longer than the operator expects, retention policy mismatch occurs.
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of shared runs.
Review vendor retention settings before use.
Use synthetic data for cross-agent testing.
Document which files may be processed by each agent.
Delete temporary artifacts after the session.
